correctness.rationale: For 1<p<infinity, the Day--James unit ball has curved strictly convex same-sign p-arcs and exactly two flat opposite-sign l1 edges. Pair sign symmetry reduces extreme candidates to nonnegative unit coordinates; comparable candidates coincide and have chord sum 2. For crossing pairs x=(a,b),y=(c,d), a>=c,b<=d, let s=a-c+d-b. If s<=2^(1/p), Minkowski bounds H<=2+s, with equality demanding proportional positive unit vectors x=y and hence s=0, impossible. If s>=2^(1/p), apply the exact split triangle estimate H<=||(a,d)||_p+||(c,b)||_p+a-c+d-b<=||(a,d)||_p+a+d<=2^(1/p)+2. Equality needs a=d=1, b=c=0. Nonextreme edge equality by joint convexity would force both endpoints to maximize with one extreme partner, contradicting the extreme classification. All signed axis pairs attain chord norms 2 and 2^(1/p). A bounded radial-sphere numerical scan for p=1.05,1.5,2,4,20 matched but was not used to prove the universal result. Source Yang--Li exact upper bound and branch were checked against its open full text.
residual_risks: p=1 excluded; p strict convexity degenerates.
